summary: Add `AirtableSource` (read-only) to MultiQuery sources, plus an `AirtableInterface` that encapsulates the full Airtable API surface (read + future write). The Source extracts records from a table id or full Airtable URL and returns a pandas DataFrame, using either an OAuth2 user token stored in the navigator_session (if present on the inbound web.Request) or a Personal Access Token fallback from `AIRTABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN`. A new aiohttp route `/api/v1/qs/integrations/airtable/callback` is registered inside `QuerySource.setup()` to receive the OAuth2 redirect and persist `{access_token, refresh_token, expires_at, scope}` into the session under the key `airtable`. Implementation follows the exact pattern established by SmartSheetSource and SharepointSource (FEAT-093 workstream): inherit `ThreadSource`, async `fetch() -> DataFrame`, raw `aiohttp.ClientSession`, navconfig-resolved credentials. Two design points are NET-NEW and need explicit decisions: (a) where session-vault writes/reads happen since QuerySource has no prior 'vault' concept, and (b) hosting/ownership of the user-facing consent page.

localization.note: Location choice — querysource/interfaces/ is the established home for cross-cutting client interfaces (http.py, credentials.py). Could alternatively live as a private module under sources/airtable.py if exposure is undesirable.
Directory `querysource/handlers/integrations/` does not exist yet — created as part of this feature.

localization.kind: modify (register callback route + optional consent route)

localization.symbol: AIRTABLE_* env constants + QS_AIRTABLE_OAUTH_ENABLED feature flag

localization.note: Only needed if we pick `pyairtable` over raw aiohttp. SmartSheet uses raw aiohttp and adds no deps.

constraints.claim: All multi-query sources must inherit `ThreadSource` and implement `async def fetch(self) -> pd.DataFrame`
Constructor signature is fixed: `(name: str, options: dict, request: web.Request, queue: asyncio.Queue)`
Credential values that look like env-var names must flow through `self.resolve_credential(key, value)` for navconfig resolution
The new Source must be registered in `SOURCE_REGISTRY` and exported in `__all__` in `querysource/queries/multi/sources/__init__.py`
Routes are registered inside `QuerySource.setup()` in `querysource/services.py`. The method name `configure()` referenced in the user prompt does not exist.
Sessions are read via `navigator_session.get_session(request, new=False)`; the project pattern memoizes on `request['user_session']`. There is no 'vault' abstraction.
Heavy/optional SDK dependencies are imported lazily inside `fetch()` and gated behind `pyproject.toml` extras (e.g. `querysource[sharepoint]`).
Source `fetch()` returns `df.infer_objects()` (or equivalently typed DataFrame) — empty result must still be a valid DataFrame, not None.

hypothesis_primary.statement: Implement `AirtableSource` as a thin ThreadSource wrapper around a new `AirtableInterface` class. The Interface holds all Airtable-specific logic (URL parsing, auth header selection, paginated record fetch, future write methods). The Source: (1) parses `options['source'].url` OR `options['source'].base_id + table_id` into base/table ids; (2) selects auth — first via `navigator_session.get_session(self._request)` checking `session['airtable']`, else `AIRTABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT via navconfig, else raises; (3) calls `interface.list_records(base_id, table_id)` and converts the list of records into a DataFrame.
hypothesis_primary.reasoning: The pattern is well-established by FEAT-093 commits (F008). The only net-new design is the dual-auth selection and the session-vault read/write — both are simple but require explicit choices documented in the proposal (not the spec).
risks: Per-user session-vault writes have no precedent in querysource; design must specify whether navigator_session is the storage or whether a separate per-user secret table is needed (e.g. for token persistence across logouts)
OAuth refresh-token flow is not handled by any existing code; the AirtableInterface needs a refresh-on-401 retry loop and a way to persist new tokens back into the session
If navigator_session is not installed in a given deployment, the OAuth path must fail gracefully (cf. defensive logging at handlers/abstract.py:248) and the source must still work via PAT-only

The user-facing consent page (`Connect to Airtable` button) is outside querysource's UI scope — the proposal must call out who owns this and whether querysource just exposes a redirect endpoint or also serves a minimal HTML page

in_scope: New `AirtableInterface` class encapsulating read + (interface stubs for) write/create-table for future use
Source URL parser supporting `https://airtable.com/<baseId>/<tableId>[/<viewId>]` and bare base+table identifiers
Dual auth: OAuth2 token from session (preferred) → PAT from `AIRTABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (fallback) → raise
New aiohttp route `/api/v1/qs/integrations/airtable/callback` registered in `QuerySource.setup()` that exchanges the auth code for tokens and stores them in `session['airtable']`
Optional `/api/v1/qs/integrations/airtable/connect` initiate-redirect endpoint that builds Airtable's auth URL and 302s the browser
Pagination handling for Airtable's `offset`-based record pagination
Field-type normalization for Airtable column types (linked records, attachments, formulas) — at minimum: flatten to JSON-serializable scalars
Optional extras entry in `pyproject.toml` (only if a real Airtable SDK is chosen)
Feature flag `QS_AIRTABLE_OAUTH_ENABLED` defaulting to off so the new routes are opt-in
out_of_scope: Writing records, creating tables, modifying schemas via the Source (Interface will expose stubs but the MultiQuery Source layer will not call them — per user clarification in Phase 0 Q&A)
Hosting the user-facing consent page HTML — querysource only provides the OAuth callback + (optionally) the connect-redirect endpoint
Persistent token storage outside of navigator_session (no new database table for tokens)
Migrating existing FEAT-091 CredentialResolver to handle OAuth tokens

confidence_map.claim: ThreadSource pattern + constructor signature are correct and stable
navigator_session is the right session backend
Per-user OAuth token writeback to session is the right storage
Raw aiohttp.ClientSession is sufficient — no need for pyairtable SDK
Refresh-token persistence on 401-retry inside AirtableInterface is the right design
Consent page is owned by frontend, not querysource

unknowns.question: When `session['airtable']` does not exist and only `AIRTABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (PAT) is configured: should that PAT be a global/server-wide credential (current FEAT-093 pattern, used by SmartSheet) or a per-user PAT (env-var name suffixed by username, à la FEAT-091 CredentialResolver)?
unknowns.user_answer: Global server-wide PAT only — matches SmartSheet/FEAT-093 pattern.

unknowns.question: Where does the user-facing 'Connect to Airtable' consent page live? Frontend-owned, or should querysource serve a minimal HTML page on `/api/v1/qs/integrations/airtable/connect`?
unknowns.user_answer: QuerySource serves a minimal HTML page at /connect so the feature is self-contained.

unknowns.question: When the OAuth access token in the session expires and refresh fails (or there is no refresh token), should the Source: (a) fall back silently to PAT, (b) raise with a clear 'reconnect required' error, or (c) attempt to clear the stale session entry and then fall back to PAT?
unknowns.user_answer: Raise a typed `AirtableReauthRequired` exception so the frontend can prompt the user to reconnect.

recommended_next_command.rationale: All three architectural unknowns were resolved by the user in Phase 5 Q&A (global PAT fallback, QS-served consent page, typed AirtableReauthRequired). Combined with high-confidence localization on the source-pattern hooks (ThreadSource, SOURCE_REGISTRY, QuerySource.setup()), the design is now concrete enough to draft a spec. The spec should hard-code the resolved decisions and call out the optional `pyairtable` SDK vs. raw-aiohttp choice as the only open implementation question.
